per_window.ps-ns: Reference state (apo P43G, 300 K, pH 6.0, 11.74 T; RelaxDB source paper doi:10.1021/bi00088a039, full text): dynamic_in_window; loop II G57-E60 has the lowest order parameters and the linker K41-S44 and C-terminal Q75 carry a slower internal component (tau_e 74-283 ps, Q75 592 ps conditional) (J12, E-r1). (Cd2+)1 P43G: loop II restricted, linker and C-terminus still flexible (J14, E-r2). (Ca2+)2 P43G, single-field reanalysis of the 1992 data: linker G42/G43 and S74/Q75 flexible, loop II restricted (J36, E-r3); the 1992 two-field averages S2 0.83 (loops), 0.85 (helices), 0.59 (linker) are abstract-only (J16, r1). Methyls split into proximal and distal classes on Ca2+ binding (J20, J21, r17, r18, abstracts); an engineered-loop mutant is stiffer than P43G (J34, r14).
per_window.us-ms: Reference state (apo P43G, 300 K, pH 6.0, single field, full text): exchange detected but unresolved by the single-field rule; 14 amides need an Rex term, A15 2.39 s-1 and D19 1.32 s-1 in loop I the largest, then K55 and V61 1.11 s-1 in loop II, attributed by the authors to intrinsic conformational heterogeneity (Ca2+ contamination below 0.5%); no rate or population (J13, E-r4). (Cd2+)1 P43G: strong exchange broadening in the unoccupied loop I (A14, K16, G18, D19, Q22; E17, S24 lost; A15, L23 unfittable), assigned to substates of the singly loaded protein, not Cd2+ exchange (J15, E-r5). (Ca2+)2 P43G: no significant exchange, 42 fitted terms all at or below 0.33 s-1 (J37, E-r6, no_evidence_in_window). Dicalcium and Ca/La P43M show millisecond equilibria in the linker (38, 42-44, 46) and site I (18, 19) by R1rho (J27, J28; r22, r23), lost in 2 M GdmHCl (J29; r39, r40), abstracts. No dispersion or R1rho study of P43G is in the evidence.
per_window.slower_than_ms: Native Pro43 calbindin (Ca2+-loaded) has two peak sets, 3:1, linked by Gly42-Pro43 cis/trans isomerism with cis-to-trans 0.2 s-1 at 25 °C (J1; r4, r9, r36; abstracts). The entry construct P43G shows no second peak set (J6; r5, r10). Wild type and P43G do not form domain-swapped dimers in crystallization drops, while P43M variants do over days (J5, J11, J31).
per_window.undetermined: Hydrogen exchange: apo amides exchange on average 220-fold faster than in the Ca2+ form, Ca2+ and Cd2+ protect many amides (J17-J19); apo P43G shows faster amide exchange and ring rotation (J7). Static or indirect: crystal cis/trans conformers (J2), minor A form fold (J3), Ca2+ off-rate 3 s-1 (J4, binding kinetics), apo, Ca2+ and Cd2+ P43G structures (J8-J10), DPC micelle and DPC binding (J22, J23), lanthanide restraints and Ce3+ substitution kinetics (J24), apo/holo comparison (J25), deamidation isoforms as an artefact lead (J26), N56A, E65Q and F36G/P43M mutants (J30, J32, J33), frozen 19F-ENDOR (J35). Not judged: Ca2+-exchange mutants M1-M4 (r25-r28), lysine methylation (r35), pseudo-EF-hand mutants (CD9K-CD9K_20261020030739-r2), Mg2+- and Mn2+-bound crystals of an unstated variant (CD9K-CD9K_20261020030739-r6, r7), E60D crystal (CD9K-CD9K_20261020030739-r8), homolog comparison (CD9K-CD9K_20261020030739-r9) and the P43MG tether-helix mutant (CD9K-CD9K_20261020030739-r16).

protein_summary.wt_apo_answer: Yes, exchange is detected in the reference state but without a rate or population: in the RelaxDB source sample (apo P43G calbindin D9k, the entry sequence, 4 mM, 300 K, pH 6.0, no buffer, 11.74 T, single field) 14 backbone amides need a model-free exchange term, largest at A15 (2.39 s-1) and D19 (1.32 s-1) in the unoccupied site I loop and at K55 and V61 (1.11 s-1) in loop II, which the authors attribute to intrinsic conformational heterogeneity after excluding exchange with the below-0.5% Ca2+-loaded contaminant (J13, full text); single-field Rex can also come from anisotropic tumbling, so the call is 'possible' and a dispersion experiment would confirm. P43G exists as a single isoform, so the two-peak cis/trans spectra of native Pro43 calbindin (Ca2+-loaded, J1) do not apply to the entry construct.
open_conflicts: Resolved on 2026-10-20: the construct of the apo and (Cd2+)1 relaxation study is P43G (p. 9833 'All current studies are carried out on the P43G mutant'; Table I title), so J12-J15 now carry the entry construct; the abstract-only rows r2 and r3 ('variant not stated') are superseded.

Native apo heterogeneity: the apo P43G assignment abstract (r11 source) says the wild type was not assigned because of conformational heterogeneity, which suggests cis/trans peak doubling also in the apo native protein, but no row shows apo peak sets or a rate.

Linker response to ions: the one-field reanalysis of the Ca2+-saturated data gives different G42/G43/S44/Q75 parameters from the 1992 two-field fit, so whether the linker stiffens on ion binding is unresolved (J36 versus J16).
questions_for_gina: Which sample is the RelaxDB CD9K entry: the apo P43G sample of the 1993 study (4 mM, 300 K, pH 6.0, 11.74 T), its (Cd2+)1 sample, or the 1992 Ca2+-loaded P43G data?

The apo P43G sample shows single-field model-free Rex at 14 amides (A15 2.39 s-1, D19 1.32 s-1) with no rate or population; the authors themselves say further kinetic analysis is not possible. Does single-field Rex count as us-ms exchange for the alternate-APO call (applied here as 'possible' with the anisotropic-tumbling caveat), and should the P43G construct be the reference rather than native Pro43 calbindin with its cis/trans two-peak state?
protein_summary.buffer_note: The RelaxDB source paper (doi:10.1021/bi00088a039) is now full text (E-rN = CD9K-CD9K_20261020211504-rN): apo and (Cd2+)1 P43G at 4 mM, 300 K, pH 6.0 adjusted with HCl, no buffer solute, 95% H2O/5% D2O, argon-purged, 11.74 T, 1 ms CPMG spacing, single field; the Ca2+-saturated data are a reanalysis of the 1992 sample whose composition is not restated. Its abstract-only rows CD9K-r2 and CD9K-r3 are superseded and no longer cited. Most other calbindin rows remain abstract-only, so their temperature, pH and buffer are unknown; r15 and r16 state pH 7.5 and 25 °C. The full-text domain-swapping work (B-r18 to B-r25) is in acidic, concentrated crystallization drops (pH about 4.8-5.5, ammonium sulfate, Ca2+, sometimes 100 mM Mg2+). The ENDOR rows are frozen at 10 K with Gd3+ in a Ca2+ site. is_wt_apo marks the apo P43G judgments (J12, J13) because P43G is the entry construct (contract rule added 2026-10-20); (Cd2+)1 and (Ca2+)2 are bound states and native Pro43 rows are a different construct. Second reads of the E rows: all six confirmed against the PDF (ledger/adjudication_pdf_batch1.json); the Claude reader flagged E-r6's class (single-field Rex assessment kept as nmr_exchange_broadening for consistency). Row-id shorthand: B-rN = CD9K-CD9K_20261020030739-rN.
